methodology: Every RULES entry in lib/contract-model/compiler/package-graph/document-classifier.ts audited for the SAME defect class: a literal single space (or comma+space) between two semantically-separate English words in a phrase pattern, matched against raw (never whitespace-normalized) text. Classified WHITESPACE_SAFE (single word, or already uses \s+/\s*), LITERAL_SPACE_RISK (fixed in this session), or INTENTIONALLY_LITERAL (none found - no pattern in this file has a legitimate reason to require an exact single space rather than tolerate ordinary line-wrap/multi-space/tab).

perPatternAudit.note: the ordinal-to-'supplemental' gap already used \s+; the 'supplemental indenture' gap did not.
the ordinal-to-'omnibus' gap already used \s+; the 'omnibus amendment' gap did not.

fixMechanism: Every LITERAL_SPACE_RISK pattern's literal inter-word ASCII space replaced with \s+ (one-or-more whitespace of any kind: space, tab, newline, CRLF, non-breaking space, etc.). Patterns are still matched against the RAW, unnormalized document text (never a whitespace-collapsed copy) - only the regex's own tolerance changed, so match indices continue to mean real text positions for the position-aware Tier 2 caption-zone/ambiguity-guard logic. This is layout-whitespace TOLERANCE, not text NORMALIZATION - explicitly the architecture the mission's own Section 4 required, avoiding the position-destroying pitfall of pre-normalizing the scanned text.
intentionallyLiteralPatternsFound: None. Every multi-word pattern in this file names an ordinary English financing-document phrase that can, in principle, be visually line-wrapped by a real source PDF/HTML rendering on any word boundary - there is no pattern in this classifier where a literal single space (as opposed to \s+) carries independent semantic significance.
